Package hadur2.core.shieldmode

Class ShieldDesign

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.shieldmode.ShieldDesign
public final class ShieldDesign extends Object
Which of Nullstride's shield differences shield mode takes (SHIELD-8 to SHIELD-12). Each is one switch, so they can be benched one at a time against the shipped mode (docs/plan-90.md, step 1; hadur-bench/build-ablation.sh). SHIPPED is what the robot runs (SHIELD-13): since 3.13, hold, learn, mode and stay, the build plan-90's step 3 swept Nullstride's list with; turn stays off. With every switch off (NONE), shield mode is exactly 3.12's.
  • hold (SHIELD-8): never fire at the enemy while shielding; the gun points at it and holds, unless the enemy is disabled.
  • learn (SHIELD-9): an enemy bullet our shield bullet met teaches the predictors its true heading, as a bullet that hit us does.
  • mode (SHIELD-10): a learned offset is the error that recurs most often, within ShieldMode.EXACT, among the last KEPT_ERRORS, not the running mean.
  • stay (SHIELD-11): no exit inside a round; the battle's exit comes once the enemy's bullets have done STAY_DAMAGE damage, or when it has not fired by tick SILENT_TICKS of a round.
  • turn (SHIELD-12): a fifth head-on base that adds the enemy's body turn on the firing tick.
  • wall (SHIELD-14): a shot whose power is uncertain (a wall hit inferred on its scan interval) builds a wave at the ledger's best-guess power instead of none. Not part of all, which stays Nullstride's five.
  • trial (SHIELD-15): every duel opponent, listed or not, starts in shield mode; an unlisted one leaves it for the battle once the shield fails Ogi's trial (see trialFails(double, int, int, int, int)). Listed opponents play as without it. Not part of all.
